title: Upload size limit is checked only after reading the entire body into memory
reasoning: The endpoint intends to cap artwork at 10MB, but it calls await file.read() with no size bound before checking len(data). A network client can force the server to materialize an arbitrarily large multipart file in memory for this route, and concurrent oversized uploads can exhaust worker memory before the 413 path runs.
reproduction: Send an authenticated multipart request with Content-Type image/jpeg and a file part much larger than 10MB. The handler reads the full file into the data bytes object before returning 413.
recommendation: Read the UploadFile in bounded chunks, accumulating into a buffer or temporary file only until MAX_ARTWORK_UPLOAD_BYTES + 1, then abort with 413 as soon as the limit is crossed. Optionally reject clearly oversized Content-Length early, but keep chunked enforcement as the authoritative check.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing artwork upload test only sends a small valid JPEG and asserts success; there is no oversized upload test proving the limit is enforced without unbounded reads.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test using a file-like object larger than MAX_ARTWORK_UPLOAD_BYTES that asserts 413 and, where practical, exercises the chunked reader path rather than a single unbounded read.
minimumFixScope: Replace the unbounded read in upload_podcast_feed_artwork with a local bounded read helper and cover the 413 path in tests/test_podcast_api.py.
